Name the four fields of development.
Gross motor; fine motor and vision; hearing, speech and language; and social, emotional and behavioural development.
In which direction does motor development proceed?
From head to feet (head control, then sitting, standing and walking), and from reflex to voluntary movement.
What is the difference between the median age and the limit age of a milestone?
The median age is the age at which half of children have the skill. The limit age is about 2 standard deviations later, by which almost all children have it.

What are the features of a bottom shuffler?
The child often skips crawling and walks late (18–24 months). It is often familial and the tone is normal. It is a normal variant.
When does the Moro reflex disappear?
What are the causes of a Moro reflex that is absent on both sides in a newborn?
Depression of the central nervous system: hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy, kernicterus, intracranial bleeding, sepsis or sedation.
What are the causes of a Moro reflex that is absent on one side?
Erb's palsy, a fractured clavicle or humerus, or a dislocated shoulder.
When does the asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR) disappear?
By 6 months. An obligatory ATNR is abnormal at any age.
When does the palmar grasp reflex disappear?
Which reaction appears at 9 months and persists for life?
The parachute reaction. It is a protective reaction, not a primitive reflex.
Is an extensor plantar response normal at 7 months?
Yes. It is normal until the child walks (12–18 months).
What does persistence of primitive reflexes after 6 months suggest?
At what age does the social smile appear?
At what age is head control achieved?
At 3 months. Head lag after 4 months is abnormal.
At what age does an infant transfer objects from hand to hand?
At what age does an infant sit without support?
At 7–8 months; the limit age is 9 months.
At what age does an infant crawl and pull to stand?
At what age does stranger anxiety appear?
At what age does an infant wave bye-bye and say "mama" and "dada"?
At what age is the mature pincer grip present?
At 12 months. An immature pincer grip is seen at 9 months.
What are the median age and the limit age for walking alone?
The median age is 12–13 months; the limit age is 18 months.
At what age is the distraction hearing test done?
At what age does a child build a tower of 2 cubes?
What are the speech and social skills of an 18-month-old child?
The child uses 6–20 words, points to parts of the body and feeds with a spoon.
At what age does a child speak in phrases of 2–3 words?
At what age does a child go up and down stairs with two feet on each step?
At what age does a child ride a tricycle?
At what age does a child give his or her full name, age and sex?
At what age does a child hop on one foot?
At what age does a child skip?
In what order, and at what ages, does a child copy shapes?
A line at 2 years, a circle at 3 years, a cross at 4 years, a square at 4½ years, a triangle at 5 years and a diamond at 6 years.

Why is developmental regression always serious?
Loss of skills already gained suggests a neurodegenerative or metabolic disease, autism or uncontrolled epilepsy.
What is the limit age for the first words?
18 months. No two-word phrases at 2 years is also abnormal.
What does hand preference before 12 months of age suggest?
Weakness of the other side (hemiplegic cerebral palsy).

What are the perinatal causes of global developmental delay?
Birth asphyxia (hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy), prematurity (intraventricular haemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia), kernicterus and hypoglycaemia.
A boy is late to walk. Which blood test is essential?
Creatine kinase (CK), to look for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
What are the social features of autism?
Poor eye contact, no pointing, no pretend play, repetitive behaviour, and delayed speech or loss of speech.
